identity.industry: Naval/Marine HVAC & Refrigeration — Defence Shipbuilding Supplier (hand-curated)

summary.oneLiner: Shree Refrigerations is a ~30-year-old refrigeration/test-equipment maker that since 2016-17 became India's premier naval/defence HVAC & refrigeration supplier, claiming **~64% market share** in defence marine AC/REF/HVAC. It is the only Indian firm with "3-of-3" naval registrations — allowed to supply HVAC, AC/REF plant AND its own control panels — and the only firm that indigenized the full submarine (Scorpene) HVAC system. Core thesis = leveraged play on Indian naval fleet expansion (150 → 230 ships), merchant-marine shipbuilding push, and AON pipeline of ₹2.3-2.4 lakh cr (~₹2,500 cr addressable for AC/REF/HVAC at ~1% of project cost), with an optionality kicker in data-centre cooling via Smardt. Guidance: 40% revenue CAGR for 3-5 yrs; ₹1,000 cr revenue / ₹120-130 cr PAT by FY30-31.

thesis: Shree Refrigerations is a ~30-year-old refrigeration/test-equipment maker that since 2016-17 became India's premier naval/defence HVAC & refrigeration supplier, claiming **~64% market share** in defence marine AC/REF/HVAC. It is the only Indian firm with "3-of-3" naval registrations — allowed to supply HVAC, AC/REF plant AND its own control panels — and the only firm that indigenized the full submarine (Scorpene) HVAC system. Core thesis = leveraged play on Indian naval fleet expansion (150 → 230 ships), merchant-marine shipbuilding push, and AON pipeline of ₹2.3-2.4 lakh cr (~₹2,500 cr addressable for AC/REF/HVAC at ~1% of project cost), with an optionality kicker in data-centre cooling via Smardt. Guidance: 40% revenue CAGR for 3-5 yrs; ₹1,000 cr revenue / ₹120-130 cr PAT by FY30-31.
scorecard (fy26 vs fy25):
| Metric | FY26 | FY25 (prior) | YoY / Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ₹153 cr | ₹~102 cr | **+50% YoY** (H2 ₹100 cr vs H1 ₹50 cr — heavily H2-skewed) |
| EBITDA margin (FY) | ~21% | 27% | Down ~600 bps — driven by spares/service falling to 7% of rev (was 30%). H2 margin 26.3%; H1 only 11% |
| EBITDA CAGR (4-yr) | — | — | ~40% CAGR over 4 yrs |
| PAT (reported) | ₹21 cr | ₹13 cr | **+64% YoY**; PAT margin 13%→14% blended (H2 PAT margin 19.3% vs H1 2.9%) |
| EPS (reported) | ₹6.47 | ₹5.00 | **+28%** despite IPO dilution (₹95 cr fresh issue) |
| **ORDER BOOK** | **₹270 cr (31-Mar-26)** | — | **~1.8x FY26 revenue**; large chunk HVAC + AC plant + REF plant. Opened FY26 with ₹215 cr orders in hand |
| Net worth | ₹219 cr | ₹118 cr | Up on ₹95 cr IPO + retained PAT |
| Net debt / leverage | Low / "not leveraged" | — | Paid off high-cost debt; interest cost H2 ₹1.3 cr (vs ₹2.3 cr H1); higher other income from IPO cash + recoveries |
| Working capital | **370 days** | 570 days | **−200 days**; receivables 350→250, inventory 250→230 days |

**One-offs / flags:** EBITDA margin drop is mix-driven (low spares share), not structural; ₹95 cr fresh IPO issue in FY26 (BSE SME/listing 2025); higher other income from deployed IPO funds; other current assets jumped ₹3.0 cr → ₹19.9 cr (supplier advances + GST input-credit stuck — 18% input vs 5% output GST on warships; refund expected H1 FY27).
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue:** 40% CAGR for next 3-5 years (CMD reaffirmed; CEO noted 50% delivered in FY26). Plant-expansion incremental rev guided at 20% CAGR (CFO) — but headline company guidance is 40%.
- **Long-term target:** ₹1,000 cr revenue and ₹120-130 cr PAT by FY30-31 (reaffirmed; management explicitly stands by ₹1,000 cr "ladder in next 5 years," not the literal ₹833 cr a flat-40% compound would give).
- **EBITDA margin:** 20-24% going forward (CFO); to improve as spares/service mix rebuilds toward 15-20% of revenue.
- **Order inflow (FY27):** ~₹1,000 cr of defence tenders expected to be floated in FY27; win rate depends on competition (current share 64%). ~60 marine tenders expected from Ministry this year.
- **H1/H2 FY27:** Less skewed than FY26 but H2 still larger (driven by shipyard delivery schedules).
- **Data centre:** Reference installation in FY27 (no revenue contribution); meaningful revenue from FY28. FY27 guidance is WITHOUT data centre.
- **Defence/naval mix:** Naval/defence remains core (~bulk of revenue); data centre + merchant marine are additive optionality.
order book & pipeline:
- **Closing order book ₹270 cr (31-Mar-26), ~1.8x revenue**; opened FY26 at ₹215 cr (bulk received in last quarter).
- 8 ongoing projects; 4 to complete in FY27, rest spill to FY28.
- Completed flagship: **P17A Nilgiri-class frigate** (oil-free compressor chiller supplied; PM-dedicated) and **Scorpene submarine** HVAC indigenization — both now spares/service annuity sources.
- Shipyards not named individually but customers are India's naval shipyards (GRSE / Mazagon / Cochin / Goa Shipyard implied via coastline offices: Visakhapatnam, Kolkata, Chennai, Goa, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi; Kochi office opening FY26).
- AON pipeline ₹2.3-2.4 lakh cr → ~₹2,500 cr defence-marine TAM for AC/REF/HVAC (~1% of project cost) over 2-2.5 yrs; +₹500 cr non-defence marine → ₹3,000-3,500 cr total marine TAM.
- Hit rate: retrofits ~100%; newbuilds — lost a few tenders (only segment with losses).
segment detail:
- **Defence/marine (core):** AC plants (4 of 6 Navy-standard capacities type-tested), HVAC (ATU all 6 type-tested, AFU/NBC filtration all type-tested, ventilation fans ~70% type-tested), control panels, oil-free compressor chillers. Revenue from new-build, retrofit, spares, and installation/AMC/lifecycle.
- **Spares & service:** Fell to 7% of FY26 revenue (was 30% FY25) — the margin swing factor; target rebuild to 15-20%.
- **Industrial/process cooling & test equipment:** Original 30-yr business; test chambers/equipment for other refrigeration firms.
- **Data centre (new):** Land-based chiller cooling via Smardt tie-up (~6 months old); oil-free/mag-bearing chiller tech same as defence.
growth / optionality:
- Indian Navy fleet 150 → 230 ships over 5-7 yrs; merchant-marine shipbuilding push (top-10 by 2035, top-3/5 by 2047) — Ministry demand aggregation rose 200 → 434 ships, projected ~700.
- Submarine/Scorpene indigenization franchise; only Indian firm with full submarine HVAC indigenization.
- **Data-centre cooling:** cooling = ~12-13% of a DC project; DC cooling market ₹/$2.99 bn → ~$9 bn over 3 yrs (~25-30% CAGR). Smardt channel partnership; reference install FY27, revenue FY28+.
- **Danfoss Turbocor TASP:** only authorized service partner in India for oil-free/mag-bearing compressors (~1,200-1,300 installed base) — strategic capability/annuity build, low near-term revenue.
- **Exports:** nascent, in marine segment only (not data centre); early discussions.
- "3-of-3" registration + turnkey ordering shift by shipyards (AC+HVAC bundled) structurally favors Shree as single-source supplier.
margins & cost:
- FY EBITDA margin 21% (down from 27%) — mix-led (low spares); H2 26.3% on operating leverage as rev doubled with flat employee/other cost.
- Guided 20-24% EBITDA; improvement hinges on spares/service rising to 15-20%.
- Metal/commodity (copper) inflation flagged as "unprecedented" — partly hedged via inflation built into multi-year fixed-price bids, but acknowledged small EBITDA drag going forward.
- Employee cost ₹7 cr → ₹21 cr over 4 yrs; future hiring/other-expense growth to lag revenue growth (operating leverage thesis).
capex:
- **Hanbarwadi (Hanbarwadi/Wajeri) Phase-1 expansion: ₹25 cr** total — mostly done, commercial production from June 2026.
- Adds ~50,000 sq ft own plant (expandable further +50,000); leased 20,000 sq ft unit closing June → total ~70-80,000 sq ft state-of-art, backward-integrated, ISO/ZED-Gold/IRS certified.
- No major capex expected for next couple of years; data-centre needs no major capex.
- **Peak revenue from existing infrastructure: ~₹400 cr** (reaffirmed from prior call); throughput non-linear with floor area due to backward integration.
capital allocation:
- FY26 IPO: ₹95 cr fresh issue (BSE listing 2025); deployed into capex, debt reduction, working-capital, and yielding interest income.
- Paid off high-cost debt; balance sheet "not leveraged."
- Future growth funded by internal accruals + bank funding (working capital is the main need); no external equity raise flagged for 40-50% CAGR plan.
- Not eligible for BSE/NSE main-board migration for ~2 more years; plans to migrate when window opens.
risks:
- **Defence-order lumpiness / H1-H2 skew** — driven by shipyard delivery schedules; numbers misleading on quarterly basis (mgmt resists quarterly reporting, prefers H1/annual).
- **Working capital** still high at 370 days despite improvement; GST input-credit lock-up (₹19.9 cr other current assets) until refund.
- **Commodity (copper/metal) inflation** beyond bid assumptions on multi-year fixed-price contracts.
- Customer concentration on Indian Navy / shipyards; newbuild tender losses.
- Data-centre & exports unproven (no revenue yet); execution dependent on partner (Smardt) product qualification.
- Single-listing (BSE) / small-cap liquidity; main-board migration gated 2 yrs.
management tone: Confident, nationalistic ("we manufacture pride"), aligned to "Amrit Kaal"/PM vision. Delivered ahead of prior 40% guidance (50% achieved). Candid on margin compression (mix), commodity drag, and tender losses in newbuilds. Receptive but firm on NOT moving to quarterly reporting (argues annual/half-yearly more accurate for defence cycle) while promising more frequent commentary. Reaffirmed ₹1,000 cr / ₹120-130 cr PAT FY30-31 target without hedging.
non-obvious points:
- Margin drop is a FEATURE of revenue surge (spares share mechanically diluted by booming equipment deliveries), not deterioration — spares is the high-margin annuity that rebuilds as completed platforms (P17A, Scorpene) age into retrofit/AMC.
- "1% of project cost" rule-of-thumb makes Shree a clean derivative of total naval/marine capex without bidding for whole platforms.
- Turnkey-ordering shift by shipyards is a quiet moat-widener: rivals who supply only AC OR HVAC must partner; Shree is single-source.
- Danfoss TASP and Smardt tie-ups are capability/optionality plays (low revenue now) but position Shree for the same oil-free chiller tech across defence + data centre + pharma.
- Working-capital compression (570→370 days) is as material to the equity story as revenue growth — funds the 40% CAGR off internal accruals.
challenges → beneficiaries:
| Challenge | Beneficiary — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shift to turnkey (AC+HVAC) ordering by shipyards | Shree Refrigerations — `—` · `544458` · Naval HVAC ⭐ | Single-product naval AC-only or HVAC-only vendors | Only 3-of-3 registered firm; bundles AC+HVAC+control panel single-source. High conviction ✅ |
| Naval fleet expansion 150→230 ships + ₹2.3-2.4 lakh cr AON pipeline | Shree Refrigerations — `—` · `544458` · Naval HVAC ✅ | Importers of naval HVAC | ~64% share, fully indigenized; ~1% of project cost. ⭐ |
| Data-centre cooling explosion (~25-30% CAGR) | Shree Refrigerations (via Smardt) — `—` · `544458` · DC cooling | — | Optionality only; revenue FY28+. Moderate conviction |

WC 570→370 days. EBITDA 21% (mix-led drop from 27%); guided 20-24% fwd. Reaffirmed 40% rev CAGR (3-5 yr) and ₹1,000 cr / ₹120-130 cr PAT FY30-31. Hanbarwadi ₹25 cr capex live June-26 (~₹400 cr peak rev capacity). New: Smardt DC-cooling tie-up (rev FY28+), Danfoss Turbocor TASP, Kochi office, export exploration (marine).
